title: The Unlocked Door
observeContent: You have been assigned to audit VulnShop's login page. The development team suspects the login form was built without proper input validation. The page contains a username field, a password field, no CAPTCHA, and no rate limiting.
testInstruction: In the Username field, enter the payload below. Leave the Password field blank. Click Log In.
identifyQuestion: What type of vulnerability did you just exploit?
identifyExplanation: The payload manipulated the SQL query structure, making the WHERE condition always true. This bypassed authentication and is a classic SQL Injection.
analyzeImpact: An attacker can authenticate as any user (including admin) without credentials. Consequences include theft of customer data, unauthorized modifications, and full account takeover.
remediationQuestion: What is the correct defense against SQL Injection login bypass?
remediationOptions: Block single quotes from input
Use parameterized queries (prepared statements)
Hash the username before querying
Add a CAPTCHA to the login form
hints: SQL treats single quotes as string delimiters. What happens if you put one inside the username field?
Try: ' OR '1'='1 in the username. This makes the WHERE clause always return true, bypassing the login.

title: The Comment Trick
observeContent: VulnShop's login query looks like: SELECT * FROM users WHERE username='[input]' AND password='[input]'. The password check might be neutralized using SQL comment syntax.
testInstruction: In the Username field, enter the payload below. Leave the Password field blank. Click Log In.
identifyQuestion: What technique did you use to bypass the password check?
identifyExplanation: The -- sequence comments out the rest of the SQL query, including the password verification. The database ignored the password condition entirely.
analyzeImpact: Comment syntax can truncate queries, bypassing authentication. Attackers can use this even when the original query structure is unknown.
remediationQuestion: What does -- do in a SQL query?
remediationOptions: It ends the query
It starts a single-line comment
It performs a logical OR
It concatenates strings
hints: Comments in SQL can cut off the rest of a query. Explore how to terminate the password check.
Try: admin'-- as the username. The double-dash comments out the password condition entirely.

title: Who Owns This Order?
observeContent: You are logged into VulnShop as a regular customer. Your order history is at /orders/detail?id=88. The application may not verify order ownership before returning data.
testInstruction: Change the order ID in the input to access a different user's order.
identifyQuestion: What vulnerability did you just exploit?
identifyExplanation: By changing the numeric ID in the URL, you accessed another user's order. The server returned data without verifying ownership.
analyzeImpact: An attacker can enumerate IDs to harvest all orders, including sensitive customer information (names, addresses, phone numbers).
remediationQuestion: How should the server prevent IDOR on the order detail endpoint?
remediationOptions: Hide the ID in a hidden form field
Verify that the order's customer_id matches the logged-in user
Use longer, unpredictable IDs
Encrypt the ID in the URL
hints: Look at the order ID parameter. Is there a number that identifies your order? What if you changed it?
Try changing the order ID to 1. The server may not check if that order belongs to you.

title: The Urgent Verification Email
observeContent: You receive an email claiming to be from VulnShop Support. The subject reads: 'URGENT: Your account will be suspended in 24 hours.' The sender is security@vulnshop-support.com but hovering the link shows http://vulnshop-verify.xyz.
testInstruction: Inspect the email carefully. Identify the red flags before deciding to click.
identifyQuestion: What type of attack is this?
identifyExplanation: The attacker created a fake login page masquerading as VulnShop to steal credentials. The domain mismatch and lack of HTTPS are red flags.
analyzeImpact: If you enter real credentials, the attacker captures them and can log into your actual VulnShop account, make purchases, or steal payment information.
remediationQuestion: What is the most reliable way to avoid falling for this phishing attack?
remediationOptions: Never click any link in any email
Always check the URL in the address bar before entering credentials
Use a password manager
Report the email to IT after clicking
hints: Check the sender's domain and hover over links before clicking. Are they the real VulnShop domain?
The link domain is vulnshop-verify.xyz — not vulnshop.com. Type REPORT_PHISHING to flag it correctly.

title: The Hidden Admin Panel
observeContent: You are logged in as a regular user. No admin links appear in your navigation. However, the admin dashboard may be accessible via a direct URL without role verification.
testInstruction: Try accessing the admin dashboard by entering its direct path.
identifyQuestion: What vulnerability allowed you to access the admin panel?
identifyExplanation: The server rendered the admin dashboard purely based on the URL, without checking whether your session actually has admin privileges.
analyzeImpact: Security through obscurity (hiding links) is not access control. Any user who guesses the admin URL can access privileged functions.
remediationQuestion: What is the correct way to protect admin pages?
remediationOptions: Change the admin URL every week
Add server-side role verification for every admin route
Only show admin links to admins
Use a secret query parameter
hints: Does the application check your role when you navigate to /admin? Try going there directly.
Try entering /admin/dashboard in the URL bar. If the page loads without admin credentials, forced browsing succeeded.

title: Retrieving Hidden Records
observeContent: VulnShop's product search returns three columns: product_name, price, description. The users table has columns: username, password_hash, email. You need to construct a UNION-based SQL Injection payload.
testInstruction: In the product search field, enter the UNION payload to extract user credentials.
testPayloadHint: ' UNION SELECT username, password_hash, email FROM users--
payloads: ' UNION SELECT username, password_hash, email FROM users--
' UNION SELECT username, password FROM users--
1' UNION SELECT username, password_hash, email FROM users--
' UNION SELECT table_name, null, null FROM information_schema.tables--
identifyQuestion: What type of SQL Injection did you perform?
identifyExplanation: You appended a second SELECT statement using UNION, merging results from the users table into the product search output.
analyzeImpact: UNION-based injection allows extraction of any data the database user has access to — including sensitive tables.
remediationQuestion: Why must the UNION SELECT have the same number of columns as the original query?
remediationOptions: To avoid syntax errors
To ensure the results can be merged
To prevent data corruption
To bypass the WHERE clause
hints: UNION allows you to attach a second SELECT statement. The column count must match the original query.
Try: ' UNION SELECT null-- and keep adding nulls until no error. Then replace with username, password_hash, email.

title: Someone Else's Profile
observeContent: User profiles are accessible at /profile?user_id=X. You are logged in as user_id=124. The application may return any profile without verifying ownership.
testInstruction: Change the user_id to access the admin's profile.
identifyExplanation: Changing the user_id parameter exposed another user's private profile. The server did not check if the logged-in user owns that profile.
analyzeImpact: An attacker can enumerate IDs to harvest the entire customer database.
remediationQuestion: How can the server prevent IDOR on user profiles?
remediationOptions: Use random GUIDs instead of sequential IDs
Check that the requested user_id matches the logged-in user's ID
Require a CAPTCHA before each profile view
Encrypt the user_id in the URL
hints: Look at the URL carefully. Is there a number that identifies your account? What if you changed it?
Try changing ?user_id=124 to ?user_id=1. If the server returns another user's data, that is IDOR.

title: Changing Your Own Role
observeContent: VulnShop passes the user's role as a URL parameter on every page request: /home?role=user. The server appears to trust this value without verification.
testInstruction: Modify the role parameter in the URL to escalate your privileges.
identifyQuestion: What vulnerability allows you to become admin?
identifyExplanation: The server accepted the role value from the URL without checking your actual session permissions. You escalated your privileges by modifying a client-controlled parameter.
analyzeImpact: Privilege information should never come from client-controlled data. The server must derive the user's role from the session.
remediationQuestion: Where should the user's role be stored to prevent tampering?
remediationOptions: In a URL parameter
In a hidden form field
In the server-side session associated with the authenticated user
In a client-side cookie
hints: The server might trust parameters it receives — even ones a normal user should not be able to set.
Try appending ?role=admin to the URL. If the server accepts it, you have escalated your own privilege.

title: The Fake Order Confirmation
observeContent: You receive an email appearing to be an order confirmation from VulnShop: 'Thank you for your purchase of an iPhone 15 Pro. If you did not make this order, click here to cancel.' The email looks professional and includes a real-looking order number. Your name is not used — it addresses you as 'Dear Customer.'
testInstruction: Identify the correct response to this suspicious email.
identifyQuestion: What type of attack is this?
identifyExplanation: The email uses urgency and a fake order to trick victims into clicking a malicious link. It is not personalized, so it is a mass phishing campaign.
analyzeImpact: Attackers use fake order confirmations to create urgency and fear. Victims act quickly and may ignore security checks.
remediationQuestion: What should you do first when you receive an unexpected order confirmation email?
remediationOptions: Click the cancellation link immediately
Forward the email to a friend for advice
Open a new browser window and type the official VulnShop URL directly, then check your order history
Reply to the email asking for more details
hints: Notice the email says 'Dear Customer' — a real VulnShop email would use your name. This is a mass phishing attempt.
Never click links in suspicious emails. Open a new browser window and navigate to the official site directly. Type CHECK_OFFICIAL_SITE.

title: The Backup File Leak
observeContent: You discover that VulnShop stores a backup file in a publicly accessible directory. The file is not linked from any page, but you can guess its name.
testInstruction: Try accessing the backup file by guessing its direct path.
identifyQuestion: What vulnerability allowed you to download the backup?
identifyExplanation: The file was stored in a publicly accessible directory with no authentication, and you guessed its name.
analyzeImpact: Attackers can discover and download sensitive files through forced browsing if directories are not properly secured.
remediationQuestion: How should sensitive files like backups be protected?
remediationOptions: Use a long, random filename
Store them outside the web root and restrict access by IP
Compress the file with a password
Only allow access from localhost
hints: The backup file is stored in a predictable location. Try guessing the path in the URL bar.
Try /backup/db.sql — if the server serves it without authentication, forced browsing has succeeded.

title: Chain of Exploitation – SQLi + IDOR
observeContent: VulnShop has two vulnerabilities: a UNION-based SQLi in the product search (which can leak user IDs) and an IDOR in the order detail endpoint. Your mission is to combine them: use SQLi to extract user IDs, then use IDOR to access their orders.
testInstruction: First use the UNION injection to extract user IDs. Then use one of those IDs in the order endpoint.
testPayloadHint: ' UNION SELECT id, username, email FROM users--
payloads: ' UNION SELECT id, username, email FROM users--
' UNION SELECT user_id, username, null FROM users--
' UNION SELECT id, username, password_hash FROM users--
1' UNION SELECT id, username, email FROM users--
identifyQuestion: What type of attack is this combination called?
identifyExplanation: You used SQLi to leak IDs, then IDOR to access those users' orders. Chaining multiple vulnerabilities multiplies the impact.
analyzeImpact: A seemingly low-risk SQLi that only exposes IDs becomes a mass data breach when combined with an IDOR that lacks ownership checks.
remediationQuestion: What is the correct remediation strategy for this chained attack?
remediationOptions: Fix only the SQLi and leave IDOR unchanged
Fix only the IDOR and leave SQLi unchanged
Fix both vulnerabilities: parameterize all queries AND enforce ownership checks
Add a WAF to block the SQLi payloads
hints: UNION injection can pull any column from any table. Target the users table to get IDs, then use those IDs in the orders endpoint.
Try: ' UNION SELECT id, username, email FROM users-- in the search. Then test the extracted IDs in the order detail endpoint.

title: Admin + IDOR Chain
observeContent: VulnShop's admin panel has a hidden endpoint /admin/all_orders that lists every order. You cannot access it as a normal user, but you have already discovered role tampering. Your mission is to use role tampering to gain admin access, then exploit IDOR on the all_orders endpoint.
testInstruction: First escalate your role to admin via URL parameter, then navigate to the admin orders endpoint.
identifyQuestion: What chain of vulnerabilities did you use?
identifyExplanation: You first tampered the role parameter to become admin, then accessed the admin-only endpoint, which gave you access to all orders (a form of IDOR).
analyzeImpact: Two Broken Access Control flaws combined: role tampering bypasses initial authorization, and missing checks on the admin panel give complete control.
remediationQuestion: How should the application prevent this chained attack?
remediationOptions: Remove the role parameter entirely
Check role only on the admin panel
Store role server-side AND verify role on every privileged endpoint
Use a different URL for the admin panel every week
hints: You already know how to tamper the role parameter. Use that first, then navigate to /admin/all_orders.
Step 1: Add ?role=admin to your URL. Step 2: Navigate to /admin/all_orders. Both steps must succeed.

title: Spear Phishing – Targeted Email Attack
observeContent: You receive a personalized email that appears to come from VulnShop's HR department. It includes your real name, your employee ID, and a link to 'update your payroll information.' The link points to http://vulnshop-hr.net.
testInstruction: Identify what makes this attack more dangerous than a regular phishing email, then report it correctly.
identifyQuestion: What type of phishing attack is this?
identifyExplanation: The email uses your personal information (name, employee ID) to appear trustworthy and targets you specifically.
analyzeImpact: Spear phishing is harder to detect because it contains accurate personal details. Attackers can bypass multi-factor authentication if victims enter OTPs on the fake page.
remediationQuestion: What is the most effective defense against spear phishing?
remediationOptions: Rely on spam filters
Use complex passwords
Treat any unsolicited request for credentials with suspicion and verify through a trusted channel
Disable HTML email
hints: This email knows your name and employee ID — that makes it spear phishing. But the domain vulnshop-hr.net is fake.
Never update credentials from an email link, even if it looks personal. Contact HR directly through the official channel. Type VERIFY_TRUSTED_CHANNEL.

title: Batch IDOR Harvest
observeContent: VulnShop added a new feature to let users view multiple orders at once via an API endpoint: /api/orders/batch?ids=1001,1002,1003. The endpoint returns all requested orders regardless of ownership.
testInstruction: Send a batch request with IDs that belong to other users.
identifyExplanation: The API endpoint allows retrieving multiple objects in one request and fails to validate ownership for any of them. This is an amplified version of IDOR.
analyzeImpact: Batch IDOR amplifies the impact of traditional IDOR. An attacker can retrieve hundreds of orders in one API call.
remediationQuestion: How should the application secure the batch API endpoint?
remediationOptions: Limit the batch size to 5 IDs
Require an API key in addition to the session token
Validate each ID against the session user ID, and return only those that the user owns
Use POST instead of GET
hints: The batch endpoint doesn't check who owns each order. Try requesting IDs that don't belong to you.
Enter IDs like 1,2,3,4,5 to request multiple orders. The server will return all of them without checking ownership.

title: The Full VulnShop Audit
observeContent: You have been appointed as the lead ethical hacker for a full security audit of VulnShop. Your goal is to demonstrate all vulnerability types: SQL Injection (login bypass and UNION extraction), broken access control (IDOR, forced browsing, role tampering, and phishing awareness).
testInstruction: Begin the audit by demonstrating the most foundational exploit: login bypass via SQL Injection.
payloads: ' UNION SELECT username, password_hash, email FROM users--
' UNION SELECT id, username, email FROM users--
identifyQuestion: What is the overarching category of all these vulnerabilities?
identifyOptions: Input validation and access control flaws
identifyExplanation: SQLi results from improper input handling; IDOR, forced browsing, and role tampering result from missing access controls. Together they constitute the two main problem areas your capstone addresses.
analyzeImpact: The combined impact of these vulnerabilities is catastrophic: an attacker could take over any account, steal all customer data, modify products, and escalate privileges to admin.
remediationQuestion: What is the single most important architectural change that would collectively prevent all these vulnerabilities?
remediationOptions: Use a Web Application Firewall (WAF)
Switch to a different programming language
Treat all user input as untrusted, use parameterized queries for database access, and enforce server-side authorization on every action
Reduce the number of features in the application
hints: This is the capstone — apply everything you have learned. Start with the most foundational exploit: login bypass.
Try ' OR '1'='1 to bypass login. This demonstrates that you understand the core SQLi vulnerability that started your journey.
